title: Receiver Behavior silent on deviceDeliveredAt suppression when receiptSharing=false
description:
Location: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md, Peer/receipt / Receiver Behavior, line ~315.

The Receiver Behavior explicitly addresses two fields when receiptSharing=false:
- readAt: MUST NOT update Message.deliveryReceipts with this value, MUST NOT deliver state-change event
- deliveredAt: MAY still record (explicitly permitted)

However, the newly added 'deviceDeliveredAt' field (Peer/receipt Request Arguments, line ~295) is not mentioned at all in the Receiver Behavior suppression logic. It is unspecified whether deviceDeliveredAt should be suppressed like readAt (it carries sub-minute timing information that could reveal behavioral patterns) or permitted like deliveredAt (it is a delivery-layer fact rather than a reading event).

This gap means implementors will make inconsistent decisions. Given that the security section (line ~1442) specifically lists 'deviceDeliveredAt' alongside 'readAt' as a timestamp that SHOULD NOT be exposed at sub-minute precision, the intent appears to be that deviceDeliveredAt is privacy-sensitive and should be suppressed along with readAt.

Correct behavior: The Receiver Behavior MUST explicitly specify the treatment of deviceDeliveredAt when receiptSharing=false, stating whether it is suppressed (like readAt) or permitted (like deliveredAt).
close_reason: Fixed: Added MUST NOT record deviceDeliveredAt when effective preference is false (federation-00.md:315)
